newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL blue chips close higher but small-caps skid.
newsitem.headline: KL blue chips close higher but small-caps skid.

text.p: Selective blue chip buying helped the key index finish on a positive note, but profit-taking and a reluctance to take pre-holiday positions kept small-capitalisation shares in the doldrums.
Some banking-related stocks attracted activity, following the collapse of two proposed mergers in the industry.

The Composite Index of blue chips ended up 5.18 points to 1,221.90, but the Second Board index slid 8.54 points or 1.40 percent to 603.11 after a mostly weaker session. Dealers said business was quiet ahead of two festivals later this week which will close the market for four week days.

"Selective blue chips are up, keeping the CI above the 1,210 support," said Ami Moris, a vice president in dealing at Capitalcorp. "Apart from the blue chips and lower liners, there's not much happening."

News about aborted bank deals involving Pacific Bank with Oversea-Chinese Banking Corp and Sime Darby with MIDF stirred heavy trading in their shares as well as in other bank-related firms, dealers said.
"I certainly don't think it's the end of bank mergers," said Dominic Armstrong, head of research at Pesaka Jardine Fleming.
